notice: Python and libraries on this page: the page's own programs (the playground, and the examples that run) run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2, while the research ran Python 3.14.6 on Linux with 2 CPUs, requests 2.34.2 and beautifulsoup4 4.15.0, and timed the free-threaded 3.14.6 build and Python 3.13.14, 3.12.13 and 3.11.15 as well. Threads in the browser: a browser's Python has a threading module but cannot start a thread (Thread.start() and ThreadPoolExecutor raise RuntimeError: can't start new thread), cannot start a program (OSError: emscripten does not support processes) and has no sockets. 4 of the 64 examples of the chapter run here, in your browser, and equal what the research recorded: they need no second thread (join before start, a lock released on error, a lock that is not reentrant, and the lock being on in the standard build, which this browser's CPython also is). The other 60 are shown as recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run, each with its reason (a thread that cannot start, a child interpreter, the local stand-in server, a web page, the timing record, or an output that differs in the browser). Stand-in: a local HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 stands in for xkcd.com; the real site was never contacted. The one picture, under the concept Fixed listing skips comics, was drawn by the deck's program; it was not made on this page. The deck, whose text is the Lecture tab, marks slides 11, 18, 20 and 23 NOT EXECUTED (slide 11: the real xkcd.com, which no program contacted; slide 18: the free-threaded build of Python 3.13, and a C extension that re-enables the lock, which is only what the documentation says; slide 20: more than 2 CPUs and a run under load; slide 23: the free-threaded build of Python 3.13, a C extension that re-enables the lock, Windows and macOS, more than 2 CPUs, runs under load and the real xkcd.com), calls slides 4, 9, 18, 19, 20, 21 and 23 Recorded (results of 14 October 2026 that it does not run again) and says on slides 10 and 11 that a local stand-in server was used.

recorded.SwitchInterval: This example sets the interpreter's thread switch interval to 0.0001 s with sys.setswitchinterval and sets it back at the end. In a fresh browser session it prints (0.005, 0.0001), as recorded, but a run that stops between the two calls (an edited program with an error, or an exercise or exam question made from it with a blank filled wrongly) leaves the session's interval at 0.0001, and the next run then prints (9.999999999999999e-05, 0.0001) instead; because the result depends on what ran before, it is not run here. It is shown as recorded under Python 3.14.6 and is not run on this page.

example_notes.title: In your browser the first statement prints the browser's Python version, '3.13.2', where the slide printed '3.14.6'; the standard-lock build (True), the thread name 'MainThread' and the active count 1 are the same. Recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run on this page.
example_notes.inc: In your browser the function compiles to 4 steps, ['LOAD_GLOBAL', 'LOAD_CONST', 'BINARY_OP', 'STORE_GLOBAL'], where the slide printed 5 steps beginning ['LOAD_GLOBAL', 'LOAD_SMALL_INT', 'BINARY_OP', 'STORE_GLOBAL']: the bytecode differs between Python 3.13.2 and 3.14.6. Recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run on this page.
example_notes.locals: In your browser the line that starts the thread raises RuntimeError: can't start new thread, because a browser's Python cannot start a thread; the slide printed False, the thread-local value being absent in the main thread. Recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run on this page.
example_notes.pins: In your browser sys._is_gil_enabled() prints True and the Py_GIL_DISABLED build variable 0, as on the slide, while os.cpu_count() prints 1 where the slide printed 2. Recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run on this page.

FixedListingSkipsComics.caption: The comic numbers 1 to 139 in rows of ten, green where the fixed downloader requested the page (125) and orange where it never did (14: 9, 19, 29 and on to 139); the first cell is empty because there is no number 0. Drawn by the deck's program fixedCut_v1_0_0.py with the small PNG writer in that program (not Pillow) after a run against a local stand-in server on 127.0.0.1; xkcd.com was never contacted; this page does not make it again.
